figures.title: What an insider reads in the provider's log after one (synthetic) clinic day
figures.caption: Each logged query embedding is inverted by nearest-neighbour search over a 60-diagnosis dictionary and joined to the appointment schedule by timestamp. ✓ = right diagnosis and right patient; ~ = right diagnosis, wrong patient; ✗ = wrong diagnosis. Your query (orange) maps to *metastatic renal cell carcinoma*. Synthetic schedule and patients.

figures.title: How coarse can the encrypted embeddings be?
figures.caption: Retrieval quality as each embedding dimension is rounded to b bits (needed to fit the cryptographic parameters). Squares = the paper's Table 1; circles = this run on the same public corpus with a small static embedder.

figures.title: What privacy costs as the corpus grows
figures.caption: Server time for both encrypted rounds (scoring + private fetch), measured on this corpus and extrapolated linearly. The paper's numbers include succinct proofs of correct computation on a 48-core machine; ours do not.
